newsitem.title: CHINA: Asia most confident in Singapore banks - poll.
newsitem.headline: Asia most confident in Singapore banks - poll.

text.p: Asian business leaders are most confident in Singaporean banks and least so in China's financial institutions, a survey showed on Wednesday.

About 67 percent of the respondents said they had the most confidence in Singapore's banks, the Far Eastern Economic Review magazine and Asia Business News television, which conducted the survey, said in a statement.
Hong Kong ranked second with 21 percent of the votes, it said. But 46 percent of those polled in Hong Kong said they had more confidence in Singaporean banks.
No respondents said they had the most confidence in banks in Thailand, South Korea, Indonesia or China.
When asked which country's banks prompted the least confidence, the business leaders said China with 37 percent of votes, followed by Indonesia with 23 percent. No respondent mentioned Hong Kong.
Singapore was also seen as the most efficient country where banking regulators identify and punish corrupt bankers. All respondents in Singapore said they were the best.
Australia followed with 82 percent of the votes.
But in Indonesia, 67 percent of respondents said their banking regulators were not efficient.
About 92 percent of those polled in Hong Kong did not think their banking sector was affected by corruption.
Overall, only 33 percent of business leaders said banks in their respective countries were entirely clean.
In South Korea, 59 percent of the respondents said their banking sector was affected by corruption "to a great extent".
The survey polled chairmen, managing directors and other top corporate executives in 10 Asian countries. The statement gave no further details about how the poll was conducted.
